title: Hierarchical Mesoporous Carbon/Silica Nanocomposites from Phenyl‐Bridged Organosilane
material_description: mesoporous carbon | mesoporous carbon obtained by removing the silica (dilute HF, ~10 wt.-%) from a mesoporous carbon/silica composite made by carbonizing (N2, 900 C, 4 h) an OTAB-templated phenylene-bridged organosilica (BTEB) hybrid
source_location: main article p. 707 (main-4.png), Figure 7, curve c (filled circles, mesoporous carbon after removal of silica), marker 1 of 35
notes: archive: fig7_curve_c.json; digitized 7.1229 mmHg (x 0.00133322 = 0.009496 bar), 23.0422 cm3(STP) g-1; wt% = W1 computed 0.0089938 x cm3(STP) g-1. Axis calibrated on 0/850 mmHg and 0/150 cm3 g-1 ticks, verified on 340 mmHg and 60 cm3 g-1 (residuals 0.56 %, 0.60 %). Curve c isolated from curves a and b with a polyline mask (work/mask_c.py); 34 of 35 markers separated, the 35th (850 mmHg end, clipped by the plot frame) is the text value row. First marker touches the y-axis; its centroid includes the axis column, so its pressure is the least certain. Sample: mesoporous carbon after HF removal of silica (Fig. 3d, Fig. 4 curve b, Fig. 6, Fig. 7 curve c); paper prints no sample code, it is named 'mesoporous carbon' in the text. Synthesis: OTAB/BTEB co-assembly (NaOH, 100 C autoclave 24 h), carbonized in N2 (20-30 cm3 min-1) at 900 C for 4 h to the carbon/silica composite, silica removed by washing with dilute HF (~10 wt.-%) for several days; class templated_carbon because the paper describes the carbon as a positive replica of the silica template. Characterization (text p. 706, N2 sorption Fig. 6): surface area 850 m2 g-1 with no method named (BET not stated), so surface_area_method = unspecified and the value sits in bet_surface_area_m2_g as the headline area; 'a pore volume of 0.50 cm3 g-1' (not stated as total; method not stated); average pore diameter 2.5 nm (method not stated; BJH is named only for the Fig. 2 samples). Composition: EDS C 99.27 at.%, Si 0.73 at.% (Fig. S2); TGA weight loss 97 % in O2 (Fig. 4 curve b), residue ~3 % (residual silica, Si is not a metal so not coded in residual_metal fields). H2 method: 'N2- and H2-sorption isotherms were measured at 77 K on a Micromeritics ASAP 2010 analyzer' (static volumetric instrument); basis not named, so uptake_type = unspecified and basis_inferred = excess by the volumetric instrumental default. No degassing, sample mass, H2 purity or free-volume calibration stated.
